The molar volume is the volume per mole of atoms. Since each mole contains \( N_A \) (Avogadro's number) atoms, the volume per unit cell is:

\[
\text{Unit cell volume} = \frac{\text{Molar volume}}{N_A} = \frac{10.3 \, \mathrm{cm^3/mol}}{6.022 \times 10^{23} \, \mathrm{atoms/mol}} \approx 1.71 \times 10^{-23} \, \mathrm{cm^3/unit cell}.

In an FCC structure, the radius \( r \) of the atoms is related to the edge length \( a \) of the unit cell by:

\[
a = 2\sqrt{2}r \quad \Rightarrow \quad r = \frac{a}{2\sqrt{2}}.
\]

The volume of the unit cell is:

\[
a^3 = \left(2\sqrt{2}r\right)^3 = 16\sqrt{2}r^3.
\]

The volume of the 4 atoms in the unit cell is:

\[
\text{Volume of 4 atoms} = 4 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{16}{3}\pi r^3.
\]

\[
16\sqrt{2}r^3 = \frac{16}{3}\pi r^3 \quad \Rightarrow \quad 16\sqrt{2} = \frac{16}{3}\pi \quad \Rightarrow \quad r^3 = \frac{3 \times 10.3}{4\pi \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}}.
\]

\[

\]

Taking the cube root:

\[

\[

\]

\[
